AUTHOR: Akgül
TITLE: Deep Learning-Based Fish Detection in Turbid Underwater Images
VENUE: 2020 28th Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU), IEEE
REGION: Çataloluk HPP vertical-slot fishway, Tekir Stream, Ceyhan Basin, Kahramanmaraş, Turkey
DATA: Own dataset: 400 frames randomly sampled from 53 five-minute videos (Camera2, Camera3) in a fishway
V_EV: Abstract (confirmed qualitatively in Sec. II-A, Turkish): 'the detection of fish in turbid and background noisy water is an important threshold to be overcome'
D_EV: Sec. II-A (Turkish): '53 videodan rastgele 400 adet video karesi seçilerek imge veri kümesi oluşturulmuştur. Bu veri kümesi %80-%20 ve %50-%50 eğitim ve test' [400 frames randomly selected from 53 videos; 80-20 and 50-50 train/test]
R_EV: Sec. III (Turkish): 'veri kümesi %80 eğitim ve %20 test; %50 eğitim ve %50 test oranlarında bir kez bölünmüştür' [dataset split once 80/20 and 50/50]
C_EV: Tables II-III (Turkish header 'Eşik Değerleri' = threshold values): mAP reported at thresholds 0,10 / 0,30 / 0,50 / 0,70 / 0,90 for each model
E_EV: Abstract: 'they are compared over the precision, recall and mean Average Precision (mAP) performances.'
METR: mAP at multiple thresholds, precision, recall
NOTE: Body text is Turkish; only abstract is English, so D/R/C evidence quotes are verbatim Turkish with English translation in brackets (rule asks for English quotes; verifier should check). Turbidity described qualitatively only ('farklı ışık koşulları, farklı bulanıklık' = different light conditions, different turbidity) with no measurement or stratified results. Frames randomly sampled from 53 videos then split randomly -> frame-level split with leakage risk not discussed. PRE: YOLO models pre-trained on ImageNet, MobileNet-SSD on Pascal VOC (no VOC option).
